function: Detection of the common and private messages of RSMA-OTFS signals in the delay-Doppler domain without SIC, by two parallel LSTM-based classifiers (p. 1, 3).
system: Downlink RSMA-OTFS: BS with Nt antennas, two users with Nr antennas (main results Nt=Nr=1, also 2), 4 GHz carrier, 15 kHz subcarrier spacing; no RIS (p. 2, 4).
method: Dual block deep learning: parallel C-DNN and P-DNN, each with LSTM, fully connected and softmax layers; supervised offline training with cross-entropy loss on transmitted-symbol labels (p. 3).
data_channel: Own simulator: delay-Doppler channel with P=4 paths, integer delay and Doppler shifts, random path phase; generated samples; no standard channel, public dataset or measurement (p. 4).
test_conditions: Training: Nt=Nr=1,2,4,8, BPSK to 32-PSK, 2 to 32 symbols, 64 subcarriers; testing: Nt=Nr=1 and 2, BPSK/QPSK, SNR sweep, 20 to 60 subcarriers (p. 3, 4, 5).
baselines: Non-learned: ML receiver with perfect CSI and SIC-based least-squares (LS) receiver; RSMA-OFDM, NOMA-OTFS, NOMA-OFDM compared as schemes; no other DL detector (p. 4, 5).
metrics: Symbol error rate versus SNR for common and private streams; rate region; training accuracy and loss; convergence time (p. 4, 5).
complexity: None for the receiver; only training convergence times in seconds (Table I, 4.58 to 43.38 s) and qualitative claims of lower complexity (p. 3, 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "The channel is modeled with P = 4 paths, characterized by specific delay-Doppler values". A custom delay-Doppler channel with random path phases; no 3GPP TDL or CDL, DeepMIMO or measured channel is named.
q2_support: p. 3: "the model needs to be retrained if the channel variations differ significantly from the training scenario". The training data already cover the tested antenna numbers and modulations; no test on an unseen channel is reported.
q3_support: p. 5: "Comparative analysis using alternative DL approaches for signal detection of OTFS-RSMA represents a promising avenue for future research". Only the non-learned ML and SIC-based LS receivers are compared on SER (p. 4); no earlier learned detector is compared.
q4_support: p. 3: "DBDL employs parallel processing, resulting in reduction of complexity". This is qualitative; Table I (p. 4) lists only training convergence times versus batch size and learning rate, with no order, operation count, parameter count or inference runtime.
q5_support: p. 3: "Training data samples are generated by considering". The data are simulated for the channel of p. 4; the letter gives no link or DOI for code or data and uses no public or measured dataset.
notes: Title and DOI checked on p. 1 (deep learning-based detection for RSMA with OTFS, 10.1109/LCOMM.2025.3538890). Area 4 (OTFS detection in the delay-Doppler domain) wins over area 1 by the specificity order. Judgement calls for the reviewer: (a) q2: Fig. 5(a) (p. 5) sweeps the number of subcarriers from 20 to 60 while the training description lists 64 subcarriers (p. 3), and the letter does not say whether the model is retrained, so q2 is not marked; (b) q4: Table I reports training convergence times only, which I did not count as the computational cost of the receiver; if a measured training runtime counts, q4 would be 1; (c) q3: RSMA-OFDM appears with the same batch-size and learning-rate sweeps (p. 4, Fig. 4(b) and 4(c)), which indicates the same DBDL receiver on OFDM, so it is a waveform comparison and not a baseline detector. Table I and the figure legends (p. 4, 5) were read from the page images.
